description.narrative:
IPU är en global organisation av parlament som bildades 1889 i syfte att arbeta för fred och mellanfolkligt samarbete. IPU består idag av 178 nationella parlamentsmedlemmar och 13 associerade medlemmar som utgörs av regionala parlament. IPU arbetar i nära samverkan med FN samt med internationella och lokala organisationer. IPU har sedan 2002 observatörsstatus i FN:s generalförsamling. Sekretariatet ligger i Genève och de har ett FN-kontor i New York. IPU’s sekretariat har idag 40 anställda.
IPU:s verksamhet syftar till att främja och stärka parlamentens lagstiftande, granskande och representativa funktioner. De har ett särskilt fokus på mänskliga rättigheter, jämställdhet, ungas deltagande och inflytande, fred och konfliktförebyggande samt parlamentens ansvar och roll i att stödja arbetet för de Globala målen för hållbar utveckling. Detta genom att skapa förutsättningar för och uppmuntra dialog mellan parlament och parlamentsledamöter världen över, genom att bedriva forskning och utveckla standarder och riktlinjer för god demokratisk parlamentarisk praxis och genom riktade kapacitetsutvecklande insatser till enskilda parlament i utvecklingsländer.

Inter-parliamentary Union (IPU) is the world organisation of national parliaments with 178 members. IPU's vision is a world where every voice counts, where democracy and parliaments are at the service of the people for peace and development. With a broad membership base IPU has the potential to reach a big majority of the world's lawmakers, and this is done through political initiatives by members and through program work initiated by the secretariat. Its political dimension enables parliaments and their members to voice their views and concerns and adopt common strategies and commitments at the international level. The political nature of the organization serves as a powerful conduit to catalyse change at national level. Discussions and debates held within the organization, often on sensitive issues, open space for dialogue and push members of parliament (MP) to engage on issues potentially sensitive in a national context. Such dialogues and debates expose MPs to diverse points of views and experiences. Added to peer-to-peer learning and influence, IPU Assemblies and political gatherings serve as platforms that encourage MPs from around the world to regularly assess their work and the work of their parliament. The resolutions adopted by the organization on those occasions serve as a framework for action and can facilitate action by parliaments at the national level. Through its programme work, IPU develops support to parliaments, focussing first on building their capacity to effectively carry out their constitutional mandate to pass laws, exercise governmental oversight, adopt budgets and represent the public.
The support is a programme support to four of IPU's five strategic objectives with a particular focus on SO1 (Effective and empowered parliaments).

The IPU's strategy 2022-2026 focuses on five strategic priorities (objectives) aimed at building effective parliamentary ecosystems and identifies seven policy goals that are a priority for parliaments and require urgent action.
SO1: Building effective and empowered parliaments SO2: Promoting inclusive and representative parliaments SO3: Supporting resilient and innovative parliaments SO4: Catalysing collective parliamentary action SO5: Strengthening the IPUs accountability (not funded by Sida)
The policy goals are to be reached through the strategic objectives. The seven policy goals have a number of formulated targets that IPU aim to strive for during the intervention. The policy goals are the following.
PG 1: Climate change PG 2: Democracy and strong parliaments PG 3: Human rights PG 4: Gender equality PG 5: Youth participation PG 6: Peace and security PG 7: Sustainable Development Goals

title.narrative: Grant Agreement between Sida and Inter- Parliamentary Union regarding Parliamentary ecosystems, for Democracy, for Everyone

description.narrative:
Overall, the IPU has achieved good results and had an important impact in a challenging environment. The Sida funded activities are well aligned with Swedish policy priorities, e.g. women and youth's political participation, support to human rights defenders and parliamentarians at risk, climate, gender equality, and capacity building of parliamentary institutions. Examples of results include:
SO1: Building effective and empowered parliaments
The IPUs Committee on the Human Rights of Parliamentarians consists of 10 parliamentarians, elected by their peers for a mandate of five years. The Committee defends MPs in trouble by raising awareness of their plight and engaging national authorities. The secretariat in Geneva carries out investigations and fact-finding missions to support the committee. Overall, the number of human rights violations against MPs continues to rise, with a total of 762 cases in 2023, up 38% from 550 in 2020.
- The Committees work in 2023 led directly to the release of nine MPs. - In recent years the IPU has enlisted the support of parliaments not currently represented on the Committee, including Germanys Bundestag, which launched a cross-party initiative in July to support MPs around the world and others at risk of human rights violations. - 32% of respondents to the IPUs annual survey of Members reported having taken specific action following IPU decisions. This rate has increased from 18% in 2020. - Over the year some 60 IPU decisions were adopted, communicated to national authorities and shared with the international community. - The IPU Committee held 20 hearings with authorities, victims, experts and other sources. - In October 2023, the IPU and UN Human Rights Office launched a toolkit to help parliaments better integrate human rights into their work.
48 parliamentarians took part in the universal periodic review (UPR), the United Nations mechanism for countries to report on human rights. This number is a welcome record for the IPU and its partners, who have been working for several years to involve parliaments more in important UN processes.
SO2: Promoting inclusive and representative parliaments
The IPUs data and knowledge on women and youth in parliament are sources for media outlets, the UN and academia. The IPU monitors developments and emerging trends, identify good practices and solutions, publish the latest research, and facilitate knowledge-sharing among parliaments when it comes to promoting women and young people in parliament. Example of results include:
- In March, the IPU published its annual Women in Parliament report, analysing global and regional data. - Also in March, the IPU and UN Women published their Women in Politics map, showing that women account for a growing number of political leaders, but also that some regions lag far behind. - With the support of the IPU a new law was adopted in Mongolia requiring that women account for at least 30% of candidates in the 2024 parliamentary elections, up from 20% at the start of the year. This quota will increase to 40% in 2028. - With IPU support Sierra Leones women MPs mobilized to raise the electoral quota for women MPs to 30%, doubling the numbers elected. - In the "I Say Yes to Youth in Parliament!" campaign, where MPs sign up to pledges to promote youth political participation, 1,500 changemakers had committed to the campaign, including 719 MPs from more than 167 countries, 61 parliamentary speakers and 15 heads of State and organizations. - In June, Mexico amended its Constitution to lower the age of eligibility for parliament from 21 years to 18. Gabon, Mexico and Zimbabwe also changed their constitutions with a view to involving more young people in their parliaments.
SO3: Supporting resilient and innovative parliaments
The IPU has a challenge getting funding for their work on climate change which is limited in scope. Even so, notable advances include:
- In 2023 the IPU launched the "Parliaments for the Planet" campaign, designed to encourage parliaments to share their good practices when it comes to greening both parliament and planet. Dozens of case studies and MP video testimonials produced by the IPU have been watched by close to 150,000 people around the world. - For the first time the IPU was inside the tent at the COP28 climate negotiations in Dubai, ensuring that parliaments were more central to the COP negotiation process through parliamentary meetings hosted in partnership with the UAE in the central COP zones.
Under the same strategic objective we find Digitalization and work on AI, both identified as crucial for parliaments for the future. Even though some work and steps forward have taken place, the IPU wishes to enhance its capacity to work with parliaments at policy and technical level in this area.
SO4: Catalysing collective parliamentary action
In 2023 the IPU held assemblies in Bahrain and Angola giving opportunity for parliamentarians from all over the world to meet and talk, including those from countries currently at war. Liberia rejoined the IPU, and the Bahamas joined, bringing the number of Member Parliaments to 180. Away from the Assemblies, IPU Secretary General Martin Chungong was also busy with direct peacebuilding efforts in Burkina Faso, Guinea and Mali, meeting the authorities and MPs to listen to their vision for the future and offer support for a transition back to democracy.
Engaging with the UN: At the opening of the 78th UN General Assembly the IPU organized its first meeting for MPs on the sidelines of the high-level week in New York. Some 48% of respondents to the IPU annual survey have carried out joint activities with UN Country Teams and/or UN agencies, up from 34% in 2021. Also - in addition to the record number of parliamentarians engaging in the UPR process - the IPU intensified its engagement with another UN mechanism the Committee on the Elimination of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW). This included outreach to parliamentary leaders and two dedicated webinars in April and December. Six countries included MPs in their CEDAW delegations. At least eight of 12 parliaments surveyed said they were now engaged with CEDAW, drafting national reports, talking with the Committee, and following up on concluding observations.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
